title: Isur

paragraphs: Mentioned in Bava Kamma 49b. According to Rashi's explanation, he and Danko were money changers. Were it not for Rashi's explanation, it would be plausible to read these as names of coins, danka and issar. See Dikdukei Soferim.[^1][^2]

notes.text: Hyman’s alternative coin-name interpretation is explicitly counterfactual: it would be plausible were it not for Rashi’s explanation of two money changers.

The intended words were not independently established at the literal Bava Kamma 49b pointer. The consulted 99b passage names Dankhu and Isur as expert money-changers, and its Rashi has Dankhi. Hyman’s 49b pointer, Danko form and counterfactual coin interpretation remain his account. His Dikdukei Soferim report was not independently collated; the comparison is not an absence proof or an accepted repair of the supplied text.
